headline: Jio's record IPO opens tomorrow as markets take a Dussehra break

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good evening, and welcome to your Market Brief for Tuesday, the twentieth of October. Markets were shut today for Dussehra, so this is a good moment to catch up before trading resumes tomorrow morning.

Three things matter most tonight. First, Reliance Jio's mega IPO opens for bidding tomorrow, and its anchor book drew more than thirty times the shares on offer. Second, the India and New Zealand free trade agreement came into force today. And third, oil is back above a hundred and ten dollars a barrel, which is weighing on the rupee and on Indian stocks.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with where we left off on Monday. It was a rough session. The Sensex fell 876 points to close at 73,852, and the Nifty slipped below 22,900. Private banks and IT stocks led the selling after some disappointing bank earnings, while public sector banks were the only sector to finish higher.

Foreign investors kept selling. They were net sellers of about 1,149 crore rupees on Monday, which was actually their smallest outflow this month. They have now sold in eleven of the twelve sessions in October. Domestic institutions bought about 3,200 crore rupees, which cushioned the fall.

For tomorrow, chart watchers are focused on 22,800 on the Nifty. Analysts say that's a crucial support level, and a break below it could open the way to 22,500. On the upside, 23,000 to 23,200 is expected to act as resistance.

One date for your calendar. Diwali Muhurat trading will be held on Sunday, the eighth of November, from 2:20 to 3:30 in the afternoon.

segments.title: Jio and the IPO rush
segments.script:
Now to the story everyone is talking about. Jio Platforms, the Reliance telecom and digital arm, opens its IPO tomorrow. At around 30,200 crore rupees, it's the largest public issue India has ever seen. The price band is 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share, and bidding closes on Thursday.

The anchor round went very well. Jio raised 8,110 crore rupees from 212 anchor investors, with LIC and Capital Group among the biggest names, and bids came in at more than thirty times what was available. Most of the money raised, up to 27,500 crore rupees, will go towards repaying Jio Infocomm's borrowings.

If you own Reliance Industries shares, there's a 2,500 crore rupee quota set aside for shareholders, so you can apply in both the shareholder and the retail category to improve your odds. Allotment is expected on the twenty-sixth, with listing on the twenty-eighth. Motilal Oswal has recommended subscribing, pointing to Jio's scale and a lower valuation than Bharti Airtel.

Jio isn't alone. Paras Healthcare's 1,450 crore rupee IPO also opens tomorrow, after raising 652 crore rupees from anchors. HD Fire Protect lists tomorrow too, with a grey market premium of around 24 percent. Next week brings EAAA India Alternatives, SFC Environmental and BLS Polymers. And OYO's parent, PRISM, is reported to be cutting the fresh issue in its IPO by nearly half, to about 3,350 crore rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Earnings season is in full swing, so here are the numbers that stood out.

In banking, brokerages are backing ICICI Bank after a strong quarter, with better profit growth and return ratios than HDFC Bank. HDFC Bank's growth was modest and its margins are under pressure, though analysts still see a recovery ahead. Union Bank of India was a bright spot, with profit up 30 percent on wider margins and lower provisions. And Yes Bank says it is evaluating ways to raise capital to support its growth plans.

Among lenders outside banking, Bajaj Finance grew profit 29 percent to 6,367 crore rupees and expects its loan book to grow 26 to 27 percent this year. Piramal Finance did even better, with profit up 67 percent, and IREDA reported 554 crore rupees in profit as disbursements jumped 31 percent.

In industry, Hindustan Zinc doubled its profit to 6,412 crore rupees on higher metal prices and output. UltraTech Cement grew profit 21 percent as cement volumes rose about 14 percent. HFCL's profit jumped more than five times. On the other side, Waaree Renewable Technologies saw profit fall 29 percent as expenses rose.

Coming up, Eternal, the parent of Zomato and Blinkit, reports soon, and brokerages expect strong growth driven by Blinkit.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
On the economy, the rupee remains the central worry. Bankers estimate the RBI has already spent about half of a 140 billion dollar foreign capital haul defending the currency, and forex reserves are down about 51 billion dollars from their September peak. The RBI is also tightening its scrutiny of overseas investments by Indian companies above a billion dollars.

Money is tight ahead of the festive season too. The RBI injected one lakh crore rupees into the banking system on Monday, its first such move since July, and will add another 50,000 crore on Wednesday. A Moneycontrol analysis of IMF data shows the weaker rupee has pushed India's five trillion dollar milestone back to 2029.

On trade, the India and New Zealand free trade agreement took effect today. All Indian goods now enter New Zealand duty free, while India has set quotas for imports like apples, kiwifruit and Manuka honey. Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in Mumbai and said a trade deal with India is very, very close. He also called India a refining superpower that could process more Venezuelan oil.

A few more numbers. India's goods trade deficit widened to 30.2 billion dollars in September. Net direct tax collections are up 13.2 percent this year, to 13.37 lakh crore rupees. And on prices, retail sugar inflation hit almost 30 percent in September, while tomato prices in Nashik crashed 65 percent in a single week because of a supply glut.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Globally, oil is the story to watch. Brent crude climbed to about 111 dollars a barrel, its highest since May, as tensions in West Asia raise supply fears. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply as attacks on ships intensify, and higher fuel prices are already sparking protests in Europe.

In Asia, the sell-off in AI and chip stocks deepened. South Korea's KOSPI fell another 5 percent and is now down 40 percent from its record high, while SK Hynix has lost 31 percent this month alone. Wall Street was calmer, with Nasdaq futures up more than 1 percent as AI shares bounced ahead of a big week of tech earnings. And China's economy grew faster than expected, putting it close to its annual target.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, some news for your own finances.

If you have a home loan, the recent quarter point repo hike to 5.5 percent has pushed up lending rates at several banks. You'll need to choose between a higher EMI and a longer tenure, and paying the higher EMI usually saves you a lot more in total interest.

On tax, a new Form 141 replaces four separate TDS forms for property purchases, rent, contractor payments and crypto transfers under the new Income Tax Act. And in an interesting ruling, the Ahmedabad tax tribunal said a 1.5 crore rupee payout from a 23-year land dispute should be taxed as capital gains, not as other income.

If you invest in gold through fund of funds, note that fresh investments into gold FoFs have been halted, to limit foreign exchange outflows. Gold itself has cooled about 26 percent from its record high.

Central government employees should watch tomorrow's Cabinet meeting, where a 3 percent DA hike, from 60 to 63 percent, is expected. And a word of caution. Zerodha's Nithin Kamath warned that pump and dump schemes run through WhatsApp tips are rising, after the Enforcement Directorate froze accounts worth about 200 crore rupees.

That's your Market Brief for this evening. Markets reopen tomorrow, the Jio IPO opens for bidding, and the Cabinet meets. Have a good evening, and happy Dussehra.
